readers.name: Early modern and modern hands, 16th–21st century (McCATMuS)
readers.langs: Portuguese, Spanish, French, Latin, Italian, English, German, Dutch
readers.about: Trained on handwritten, printed and typewritten documents from the 16th to the 21st century. The best free choice for Inquisition records, notarial deeds and letters.
readers.cite: Chagué, Alix (2024). McCATMuS - Transcription model for handwritten, printed and typewritten documents from the 16th century to the 21st century. Zenodo. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.13788177

readers.name: Medieval book hands, 8th–16th century (CATMuS Medieval)
readers.langs: Latin, French, Spanish, Italian, Catalan, Occitan, Dutch, Venetian
readers.about: Trained on over 200 medieval manuscripts: caroline, gothic textualis, cursiva, hybrida and humanistic scripts. Keeps abbreviations as written (MUFI characters).
readers.cite: Pinche, Ariane, Clérice, Thibault, Vlachou-Efstathiou, Malamatenia, Chagué, Alix et al. (2025). CATMuS Medieval. Zenodo. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.15030337

readers.name: Medieval and early modern documents, charters and registers (TRIDIS)
readers.about: Trained on documentary manuscripts (charters, registers, accounts) and expands abbreviations into full words.
readers.cite: Torres Aguilar, Sergio, Jolivet, Vincent (2024). TRIDIS: HTR model for Multilingual Medieval and Early Modern Documentary Manuscripts (11th-16th). Zenodo. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.10800223

readers.name: Portuguese Inquisition records, 16th–19th century (TraPrInq)
readers.about: Trained on over 6,400 pages of Portuguese Inquisition trials (Lisbon, Coimbra, Évora) transcribed by the TraPrInq project. Made for Inquisition records.
readers.cite: Weslley Oliveira (2024). TraPrInq - Transcription model to recognize Portuguese handwritten texts from the 16th to 19th centuries. Zenodo. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.14538271

readers.name: Portuguese parish registers, 18th–19th century (GeneaPT)
readers.about: Trained on baptism, marriage and burial registers from Portuguese parishes. Made for genealogy.
readers.cite: GeneaPT (2026). GeneaPT – Kraken HTR model for Portuguese parish registers (18th–19th c.). Zenodo. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23733764
